Subject: Unit economics deep-dive: pricing and token volume follow-up

Thanks again for taking the time today, Emily — really appreciated the candid convo and product walkthrough. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Recap: FintechX wants to add a contextual assistance feature in your payments UX (auto-summarize disputes, suggest reconciliation steps). Pilot target = 50–100k monthly active users, expected 10M tokens/month initially.
- Asks for Redwood: confirmed token-volume profile (pilot, steady-state, peak), target budget range, and any margin or CAC constraints you want us to model.
- Next steps: I pulled a preliminary pricing spreadsheet (attached) with a few price tiers; if you can confirm volumes/budget we’ll convert to a tailored commit proposal.

A few clarifying Qs to help our unit-econ model:
1) For pilot: would 10M tokens/month be a firm expectation or a best-guess range?
2) What monthly budget range should we target for the pilot (ballpark $/month)?
3) Any internal target for $/1M tokens or a maximum unit cost you need us to hit to keep feature economics positive?

I attached a short model (pricing_proposal_v2.xlsx) and a CSV with the quick unit-econ assumptions (unit_econ_model.csv). Rishi will join the deep-dive to cover latency/cost optimizations (quantization, batching, caching).

If it works, I’ll schedule a 60-min unit-econ deep-dive next week (Rishi + Lauren + me). Proposed times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks — talk soon.

Thanks Marissa — great call. A few answers and clarifications below: 

- Token volumes: current best guess is: pilot ~10M tokens/month (we expect ~50k MAU with average session ~200 tokens); steady-state (6–12 months) 15–20M tokens/month; peak during promos or new feature rollouts could reach 40–60M tokens/month.
- Budget: pilot budget is roughly $20k–$35k/month; if economics look great we can expand commit to $40k–$60k/month during steady state.
- Target unit cost: our internal product/finance team has signaled we’d like to target <= $50 per 1M tokens equivalent cost from vendors to keep per-feature margins healthy, but we’re flexible if you can show favorable downstream unit econ.

Follow-ups: 
- We’ll need an example of $/feature (cost per invocation), and a simple CAC payback example (we typically target < 6 months payback for new features).
- Can you show a scenario that maps tokens -> cost -> price per invocation -> gross margin?

Cc’ing Alex (product) and procurement so they see the numbers early. Happy to take the deep-dive next Wed 10am PT if that works for your team.
\Best,
Emily

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-04T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive: pricing and token volume follow-up

Great — thanks for the detail, Emily. I put together a compact back-of-envelope mapping below to help illustrate how token pricing translates to $/feature and CAC payback. I’ll walk through these in the deep-dive and we’ll share the spreadsheet with scenario toggles.

Assumptions (example scenario):
- Price tier example (hosted API list/indicative):
  • Pilot (no commit): $80 per 1M tokens
  • Mid-commit: $55 per 1M tokens
  • High-commit (annual): $40 per 1M tokens
- Cost per token derived from above: $80/1M = $0.00008 per token; $55/1M = $0.000055; $40/1M = $0.00004.
- Typical invocation for your feature: 200–300 tokens (we’ll use 250 tokens avg).

Computed metrics (per-invocation):
- Pilot cost (250 tokens * $0.00008) = $0.02 per invocation
- Mid-commit cost (250 * $0.000055) = $0.01375 (~$0.014) per invocation
- High-commit cost (250 * $0.00004) = $0.01 per invocation

Customer pricing examples and margins (illustrative):
- If FintechX prices the feature at $0.10 per invocation: 
  • Pilot gross margin = (0.10 - 0.02)/0.10 = 80%
  • Mid-commit margin = (0.10 - 0.01375)/0.10 = 86.25%
  • High-commit margin = (0.10 - 0.01)/0.10 = 90%

CAC payback (illustrative):
- Example: if incremental CAC to acquire feature users = $100 per user; ARPU (incremental revenue) from feature = $5/month -> payback = 20 months (too long).
- If ARPU = $25/month, payback = 4 months (within your <6 month target).

Unit-econ levers we can work on together:
- Reduce cost: quantization + reduced context windows for some calls, batching, prefix caching for repeated prompts. Rishi can show ops levers that reduce $/1M effective cost.
- Increase price/ARPU: bundling the feature into a higher-tier plan or adding tiered limits.
- Improve CAC: trial-to-paid flows, in-app conversion nudges, referral credits.

Attached is a simple model (unit_econ_model.csv) that lets you change tokens per invocation, price per invocation, CAC and see payback. If you want, we’ll prepare a version mapping to your 50k MAU pilot expectations (I can plug your numbers in if you confirm MAU/session rates).

Proposed next step: confirm Wed 10am PT for the deep-dive. Rishi — can you bring a short ops deck (3 slides) showing batching/quantization impact on $/1M tokens? Lauren — can you bring renewal/expansion playbook notes so we can model ARPU/CAC improvements?

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 10am PT once Emily confirms.
\--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
\[Attachment: unit_econ_model.csv (CSV, 6KB)]
